narrativeReportMd:
# ElementDefinition R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. The highest-impact local R4-to-R6 issue is removal of `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath`; additional risks come from changed choice type domains, a new binding invariant, tighter local constraints, and R6-only metadata that cannot round-trip to R4.

## Scope
The assigned R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions were present and compared directly. Inherited-only base-artifact changes were excluded.

## Main migration themes
Remove/archive XPath constraints, regenerate models for changed choices and markdown fields, update enum/terminology handling, and define an R6-to-R4 preservation strategy for `binding.additional`, `constraint.suppress`, `mustHaveValue`, and `valueAlternatives`.

## Highest-impact findings
`constraint.xpath` removal is the clearest hard break. R6-only additional binding metadata is the largest round-trip risk.

## Findings requiring human review
Review external IG prevalence for removed Contributor choices and sparse bindings, verify terminology expansions, and review R6 conformance pages for obligations and slicing semantics.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several changes are justified by cleaner R6 modeling, but deprecated fields, warning phases, or official cross-version extensions would reduce disruption.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: ElementDefinition has material local R4-to-R6 breaks: removed XPath constraints, changed value choice domains, and stricter binding/path constraints. R6-to-R4 risk is high for new additional binding and primitive value metadata. Structural confidence is high; terminology and prevalence confidence would improve with official expansions and external IG scans.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Update validators and generated models, remove or externalize XPath, scan for sparse bindings and removed choice suffixes, and preserve R6-only metadata through extensions or sidecar mappings when converting to R4.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: High for computable StructureDefinition deltas because both assigned files were present and compared. Medium for terminology semantics, official rationale, and real-world prevalence because no official diff, live terminology expansion, or external IG corpus was available.

findings.title: ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath was removed

oldState.summary: R4 allowed an optional XPath expression on each constraint.
oldState.narrativeMd: `constraint.xpath` carried an XML/XPath form of an invariant.

newState.narrativeMd: The surrounding `constraint` backbone remains, but `xpath` is absent.

facts.note: Present in R4 differential/snapshot; absent in R6.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Neighboring constraint children are retained, so this is removal rather than rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances that populate `constraint.xpath` become invalid against R6 because the child no longer exists. Runtime/codegen impact is high for models and validators exposing or using the XPath property; 656 local R4 core StructureDefinition files contain `xpath`.

justification.inferredGoal: Remove a format-specific constraint language in favor of FHIRPath.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `constraint.xpath` in base R6 as a deprecated legacy field for a transition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: R4 already warned that XPath was generally not useful outside XML and might be removed, and FHIRPath is the cross-format constraint language. The breaking removal is therefore probably justified, but only after recognizing that a base-design transition path existed. Keeping the field would reduce immediate data loss, yet it would materially weaken the cleanup by keeping a deprecated representation in active ElementDefinition instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base R6 design would have retained `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath` as deprecated, non-preferred legacy metadata while requiring or strongly preferring `constraint.expression` for normative validation. That preserves old R4 definitions, but it leaves two same-resource representations for constraints and risks indefinite XPath authoring/support rather than completing the migration to FHIRPath.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve R4 instances but retain an XML-only constraint surface and a dual-language validator/tooling burden that could persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `constraint.xpath` as 0..1 string.
R6 omits `constraint.xpath` while retaining `expression` and `source`.
656 local R4 core StructureDefinition files contain an `xpath` member.

examples.examplesMd: Illustrative fragment only; keep or author FHIRPath and remove/archive XPath.

findings.narrativeMd: `ElementDefinition.constraint.xpath` is a direct local hard break. Strict R6 parsers and generated classes have no slot for the R4 XPath member.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid when an R4 ElementDefinition contains `constraint.xpath`. R6-to-R4 is not a problem for this field because R6 no longer emits it.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan StructureDefinitions for `constraint.xpath`; verify each invariant has an adequate FHIRPath `expression`; preserve unmatched XPath only outside the core R6 model.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The removal is technically justified but could have been staged with deprecation or a standard legacy extension.

findings.title: R6 adds local ElementDefinition metadata not representable in R4

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 cannot natively carry these ElementDefinition metadata concepts.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional additional binding, warning suppression, and primitive value-replacement metadata.
newState.narrativeMd: These element IDs are in the R6 ElementDefinition differential, so they are local additions.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Absent from R4 snapshot/differential and present in R6 under existing local parents.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The additions are optional, so existing R4 definitions still move forward. R6 definitions using them lose native meaning in R4; `binding.additional` is already used in 160 local R6 core StructureDefinitions.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent richer terminology and validation metadata directly.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative applies because these are optional R6 additions that preserve R4-valid ElementDefinition instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The added fields make additional bindings, warning suppression, and primitive value-presence rules first-class in R6 without making existing R4 content invalid. The reported risk is real for R6-to-R4 round-tripping, but it is not an R4-to-R6 breaking base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A standard R4 extension bridge could preserve `binding.additional`, `constraint.suppress`, `mustHaveValue`, and `valueAlternatives` when exporting R6 definitions to R4. Under the calibration rules, that is conversion tooling/backport strategy, not a backward-compatible alternative to the R6 base model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 conversion still needs extensions or sidecar metadata, but that is a down-conversion mitigation rather than a less-breaking R6 base design.

evidence.detail: R6 adds `binding.additional` with required `purpose` and `valueSet` inside each repeat.
R6 adds `constraint.suppress` as 0..1 boolean.
R6 adds primitive value presence/value alternative metadata.
160 local R6 core StructureDefinition files contain `binding.additional` arrays.

examples.examplesMd: R4 needs extensions or sidecar metadata to preserve these R6 children.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 makes additional bindings and primitive value rules first-class. This is mainly a round-trip and codegen risk, not a forward validation break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Strict R4 validators/classes reject or drop these children. Dropping `binding.additional` can alter terminology guidance and validation behavior.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For R6-to-R4, map these fields to governed extensions or sidecar metadata and test additional-binding preservation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: First-class R6 fields are cleaner than extensions, but a standard cross-version extension bridge would be more backward-compatible.

findings.title: Choice type domains changed for value constraint elements

oldState.summary: R4 broad value choices include `Contributor` and lack several R6 datatypes.
oldState.narrativeMd: `Contributor` is allowed for default/fixed/pattern/example value choices.

newState.summary: R6 removes `Contributor` and adds R6 datatypes including `integer64`.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds these types to default/fixed/pattern/example; `integer64` is also added to min/max value choices.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same choice elements remain; only type arrays changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 definitions using `fixedContributor`, `patternContributor`, `defaultValueContributor`, or `example.valueContributor` have no R6 choice arm. R6 definitions using new choice suffixes such as `minValueInteger64` are not natively R4-representable. Core-package prevalence for Contributor choice use appears rare.

justification.inferredGoal: Align value choices with the R6 datatype inventory.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `Contributor` choice arms, likely with a deprecated legacy `Contributor` datatype or explicit legacy value arm.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding R6 datatype choice arms is necessary and forward-compatible. The disruptive part is removing `Contributor`, which is absent from the R6 datatype inventory and appears unused in the local R4 core corpus. A compatibility arm could protect external IGs, but it would materially compromise the goal of aligning ElementDefinition value choices with the actual R6 type system.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep `defaultValueContributor`, `fixedContributor`, `patternContributor`, and `example.valueContributor` as deprecated legacy choices. That is only a partial alternative because R6 would also need to preserve or emulate the retired `Contributor` shape, and both old and replacement representations could remain in circulation indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve rare old choice suffixes but keep obsolete same-resource representations and datatype inventory debt alongside the R6 replacements.

evidence.detail: R4 includes `Contributor` in broad value choices.
R6 omits `Contributor` and adds R6 datatypes.
R6 adds `integer64` to min/max value choices.

examples.examplesMd: Contributor use is likely rare, but the choice suffix removal is structurally breaking when present.

findings.narrativeMd: Choice suffixes are part of the serialized and generated model surface. The allowed suffix set changed in both directions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Hard R4-to-R6 only for removed Contributor choice arms; R6-to-R4 risk for any newly added R6 choice arm.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan for affected choice suffixes. Map Contributor manually; preserve new R6 choices as extensions/sidecar data when converting to R4.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding choice arms is forward-compatible; removing Contributor could have been softened through deprecation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No Contributor choice occurrences were found in the local R4 core package; external IG prevalence is unknown.

findings.title: ElementDefinition.binding must now have a description or valueSet

oldState.narrativeMd: A binding with only mandatory `strength` was structurally valid in R4.

newState.summary: R6 adds an error invariant requiring description or valueSet.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires useful binding content and adds a rule for the new `descriptive` strength.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Same local `binding` element; new R6 constraints.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A sparse R4 binding with only `strength` is old-valid/new-invalid under R6 `eld-23`. No such bindings were found in local core packages, so expected prevalence is rare.

justification.inferredGoal: Ensure every binding has computable or narrative content.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Introduce the description-or-valueSet requirement first as a warning or best-practice rule.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is strong: a binding with only `strength` is underspecified and hard for tools or readers to use. The hard error is probably justified because remediation is straightforward and no sparse bindings were found in the local core corpus. A softer transition would reduce breakage but would leave ambiguous bindings valid in base R6.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep sparse bindings valid while adding a warning, best-practice invariant, or publisher QA rule encouraging `description` or `valueSet`. That alternative is incomplete because validators could not rely on R6 base conformance to ensure usable binding content.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This preserves sparse R4 bindings but does not guarantee that base R6 bindings carry meaningful narrative or computable terminology content.

evidence.detail: R4 has no description-or-valueSet invariant.
R6 adds `description.exists() or valueSet.exists()`.
No local core bindings missing both fields were found.

binding.description: Example codes suitable for this element.

examples.examplesMd: R6 requires adding at least description or valueSet.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 tightens the binding content model. Sparse R4 bindings need enrichment before strict R6 validation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old-valid/new-invalid for bindings with neither description nor valueSet; the wire field names are unchanged but invariant validation fails.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Scan bindings and populate a real `valueSet` or meaningful markdown `description`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A warning-level transition would have preserved backward compatibility while encouraging better bindings.

findings.title: ElementDefinition path and modeling constraints were tightened

oldState.summary: R4 had local path syntax and code-generation warnings.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 `eld-19` regex was less explicit in the computable expression.

newState.summary: R6 anchors the path regex and adds local modeling warnings.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 makes path syntax more explicit and warns about fixed-vs-pattern, ordering, mapping identity, and multiple bindable types.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Root-level local constraints on the same ElementDefinition element.

impact.impactRationaleMd: External artifacts with permissively accepted path forms can fail R6 `eld-19`; warning additions can also break CI pipelines that treat warnings as errors. No failing paths were found in the local R4 core package.

justification.inferredGoal: Make path syntax and modeling guidance reliable for validators/code generators.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Phase in the anchored path rule and new modeling checks as warnings before enforcing them as base errors.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The anchored `eld-19` expression appears to make the stated path rule computable rather than changing the intended model, and the added warnings target known authoring/codegen problems. Because external artifacts may have relied on the looser R4 expression, a staged warning path was possible, but it would materially delay the interoperability and tooling cleanup.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would keep the old error invariant, add the anchored check as warning or best-practice guidance, and promote it later. That is only partial because it would not let R6 validators depend on the stricter path syntax from the base definition.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This protects permissively accepted R4 definitions but prolongs path/code-generation ambiguity and leaves problematic models conformant for another cycle.

evidence.detail: R4 `eld-19` has a less explicit path regex.
R6 anchors the path regex and states 64-character component rules.
R6 adds local warning-level constraints.

examples.examplesMd: No concrete failing core-package example was found; validate external IG paths and warning policies.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 tightens local constraints that protect code generation and model quality.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: `eld-19` is an error and can make old definitions invalid; new warning constraints can affect QA gates.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Run R6 validation over all StructureDefinitions and normalize non-standard paths or warning escalations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stricter rule improves interoperability but could have been phased in as warning-only.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Impact depends partly on FHIRPath regex semantics in the validator used for R4.

findings.title: Enum-like terminology domains changed

oldState.summary: R4 binding strength has four codes, discriminator type has five codes, and type.code binds to defined-types.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 enum-like values include binding strengths required/extensible/preferred/example and discriminator types value/exists/pattern/type/profile.

newState.summary: R6 adds `descriptive` binding strength, `position` discriminator type, deprecates `pattern`, and changes type.code binding.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Compared local CodeSystem concepts, not live expansions.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 values are valid only with R6 terminology and updated enum handling.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Same element IDs with changed bindings/code systems.

impact.impactRationaleMd: No inspected required binding removed old codes, so R4 values generally remain accepted in R6. R6 values such as `descriptive` and `position` are not R4-representable and can break closed enum switches.

justification.inferredGoal: Support R6 additional-binding and slicing semantics.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative applies because observed R4 required codes remain accepted; the main changes add R6 codes or deprecate without removal.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The terminology changes support R6 additional-binding and slicing semantics while preserving the R4 codes observed in the required domains. `pattern` remains present, though deprecated, and new values such as `descriptive` and `position` are additive from the R4-to-R6 instance perspective.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: ConceptMaps, enum shims, or R4 extensions can help older tooling process new R6 values, but they do not represent a less-breaking R6 base design for R4-valid ElementDefinition instances because the base change does not remove the old enum values.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Closed-enum tooling and R6-to-R4 mappings still need updates, but those are runtime/down-conversion mitigations rather than a less-breaking base design.

evidence.detail: R6 adds code `descriptive`.
R6 adds `position` and marks `pattern` as deprecated/same as `value`.
R6 changes `type.code` binding to `elementdefinition-types`.

examples.examplesMd: R4 enum-based tooling will need explicit mappings for these R6 values.

findings.narrativeMd: ElementDefinition terminology domains are often compiled into enums. R6 expands/redirects several of them.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 is not a hard break from observed code removals. R6-to-R4 and runtime enum handling are the main risks.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate enums and validators; map `pattern` discriminator semantics to `value` where appropriate; do not use R4 `defined-types` as the R6 `type.code` universe.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding codes is safer than removing them but still breaks closed-enum consumers; ConceptMaps or compatibility shims are advisable.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A live terminology expansion would improve confidence, especially for `elementdefinition-types`.

findings.title: Three descriptive fields changed from string to markdown

oldState.summary: R4 uses `string` for binding.description, constraint.requirements, and mapping.comment.
oldState.narrativeMd: These fields are plain strings in R4.

newState.summary: R6 uses `markdown` for the same fields.
newState.narrativeMd: Property names and cardinalities are unchanged; primitive type metadata changes.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Same element IDs; primitive type changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Plain JSON values remain strings, but generated primitive wrappers, validators, and renderers must distinguish markdown from string.

justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the fields typed as `string` and clarify in their definitions that markdown content is allowed or expected.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of marking documentation-oriented fields as markdown is reasonable, and the wire-level break is low because JSON values are still strings. However, the old `string` shape could have carried markdown text with clearer definitions, so the type change was not the only possible design. The alternative is incomplete because it would not give tools a normative primitive type signal for markdown handling.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would leave `binding.description`, `constraint.requirements`, and `mapping.comment` as `string` while updating definitions and rendering guidance to say that markdown may be used. That preserves most R4 APIs and instances, but it relies on path-specific knowledge rather than the FHIR primitive type system.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve generated API compatibility but lose computable markdown primitive semantics, renderer/validator signaling, and consistency with other markdown documentation fields.

evidence.detail: R4 type is string.
R6 type is markdown.
R6 also changes these fields to markdown.

examples.examplesMd: No normal JSON string transform is required; update generated property types and markdown rendering.

findings.narrativeMd: This is a low-impact API/type metadata change rather than a structural wire break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Plain strings remain parseable; differences arise in primitive type validation, extensions, and rendering.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Regenerate models and test markdown rendering/escaping for these fields.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is effectively backward-compatible at the wire level.

findings.title: Conformance guidance changed for mustSupport, fixed/pattern, XML attributes, and slicing

oldState.summary: R4 text uses mustSupport as the main support flag and lacks several R6 clarifications.

semanticText.definition: If true, implementations SHALL provide support for the element.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 guidance does not include the obligations phase-out language.

newState.summary: R6 says mustSupport is being phased out by obligations and clarifies several constraint semantics.

semanticText.definition: mustSupport is being phased out and replaced by obligations.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 clarifies fixed/pattern behavior, xmlAttr extension prohibition, and discriminator `pattern` deprecation.

facts.newValue: being phased out and replaced by obligations

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Existing local elements with changed definitions/comments.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Structural validation usually remains unchanged, but profile authoring, QA warnings, conformance documentation, and validator behavior may shift.

justification.inferredGoal: Clarify ambiguous conformance semantics and guide authors toward R6 obligations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Stage the changed conformance semantics as additive guidance or warnings before making stronger normative statements.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 clarifications address real ambiguity in profile authoring and validation behavior, so the direction is probably justified. A gentler transition could have reduced surprise for R4-derived policy and test suites, but it would not provide the same immediate base-level clarity.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking design would present obligations, fixed/pattern interpretation, xmlAttr extension restrictions, and `pattern` discriminator deprecation as transitional guidance or warnings while retaining older conformance wording for compatibility. That is only partial because it delays convergence on the clarified R6 semantics and leaves validators/publishers with weaker shared expectations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve R4 assumptions longer but prolong ambiguity around obligations, fixed/pattern behavior, xmlAttr extensions, and discriminator semantics.

evidence.detail: R6 says mustSupport is being phased out and replaced by obligations.
R6 adds `if present` and occurrence-oriented wording.
R6 says no extensions are allowed on `xmlAttr` elements.
R6 says `pattern` discriminator is deprecated and same as `value`.

examples.examplesMd: Semantic finding; validate publisher QA output and conformance documentation rather than a single JSON fragment.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 changes how several stable ElementDefinition fields should be interpreted by authors and tools.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Instances usually remain structurally valid, but warning output, fixed/pattern interpretation, and support obligations can change.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Review profile authoring rules and tests involving mustSupport, obligations, fixed/pattern, xmlAttr, and discriminator `pattern`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Clarifying prose is useful, but explicit transition guidance would be more backward-compatible.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Narrative conformance pages and obligation profiles were not reviewed.

No local isSummary flag changes were found on existing elements; new R6 summary elements are covered as additions.
